gap: None of the result pages I could open (keebspicks, Notebookcheck, HLPlanet) states that Gamakay's own first-generation magnetic switches fit only the TK75HE V1 and that Gamakay names the TK75HE V2 as the board for other brands' magnetic switches; I could not check the remaining results, so 'no result' is not established.
standout_why: Compared against keebspicks (cited), Notebookcheck's HE75 Mag review (cited) and HLPlanet's Hall effect guide. keebspicks already does this kind of cell for other boards: it says the Aula F75 HE is 8,000 Hz wired but 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz, and that the Keychron K2 HE takes Gateron double-rail switches only. Notebookcheck already has the HE75 Mag's wireless limit (1,000 Hz max tested on wireless, repeated inputs on 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth). HLPlanet says only 'every HE keyboard is hotswappable' and names the stock switches; the fetch also read its table as listing the Yunzii RT75 Pro as '1000Hz polling, wired only', which conflicts with Yunzii's page. None of the three has the Gamakay V1/V2 switch split or Yunzii's own 0.1 ms wired / 1 ms wireless figures. PC Gamer and Tom's Guide (both cited) came back truncated to navigation, and the other results were not opened, so rivals may hold more than I saw. Maker product pages for most candidates returned HTTP 429, so the per-mode grid is incomplete.
decides: It does not decide the pick. It confirms the TK75HE V2 (not a discounted V1) as the Gamakay board to buy if the shopper wants to swap in other brands' magnetic switches. It also tempers ChatGPT's 'best wireless gaming' case for the Yunzii RT75 Pro: Yunzii states 8K on 2.4 GHz but 1 ms wireless latency against 0.1 ms wired. Epomaker calls the HE80 a wired keyboard, so it is out for anyone who needs wireless.
